title: THE Best Task Manager
body: I absolutely love Sunsama on desktop and the mobile experience is great as well. This is my go-to planning app to keep my days organized and stress-free. Cannot recommend enough!
author: logannlanee

title: Essential
body: Of all the apps I’ve ever tried, this is the only one I’ve never cancelled and use every single day.
author: ty douglas c

title: can’t log in
body: keep receiving message of failed to log in
author: M1201C

title: Excellent application
body: This app is the best of its kind that I’ve used. The flow, the UI, everything makes sense and works beautifully. It was a serious life changer during law school. The creator of the app also seems to be a swell person. I’ve been using the app for a while and they’ve periodically reached out to me  to ask about my experiences, offer support, and solicit feedback.
author: DocCapps

title: Faithful user for years
body: The system works. Wouldn’t use anything else.
author: Tpalmer75

title: I wish it was it
body:
I have ADHD and work as a founder of a healthcare company. Not every productivity system app will suit my needs. I require something reliable, bug-free, and highly mobile-friendly, considering my frequent on-the-go lifestyle.

Lately, the mobile app has been plagued with numerous bugs. For instance, planned times don’t persist, task names can’t be changed, duplicate tasks are added to the calendar, and more. Compared to alternatives like TickTick, Sunsama loses its appeal when priced at $20.00 per month and still has these issues.

Sunsama, while user-friendly, has redundant buttons that lack labels, making navigation cumbersome and not truly user-friendly.

On the other hand, I can pay around $35 for a whole year of TickTick without encountering any issues. What I appreciate about Sunsama is its intentional approach to planning and shutdown, allowing me to plan with purpose. However, this intentionality alone doesn’t justify the higher price when the app has persistent bugs.

In my opinion, I need a workhorse productivity app, not a designer one.
author: LIFEOFWDNS

title: Absolutely awesome
body: This app has been life changing for me. I get more done each week than I used to in a month.  I’ve been using it for years and the tech has improved greatly while still focusing on GSD.  Couldn’t be better for someone looking to improve their time management and productivity.
author: Oldirtybaffler

title: Perfect
body: I’ve tried a ton of similar apps over the years and keep coming back to Sunsama. It implements all of the features that work for my flow better than anything else.
author: veeerymuch

title: Clean and focused
body: Best task manager app I’ve found; integrations are great with calendar and the flexibility helps me use it as I want and it adds a little peace and order to my hectic work schedule of changing priorities and tasks
author: JohnW55.1

title: ADHD Relief
body:
I’ve been using Sunsama since 2021. It has been invaluable for managing time. It was so helpful that I asked my work to approve the Asana integration so that I can time block work AND personal life in one view.

FYI the DESKTOP version is where the real power is at. Although the mobile version has most of the same basic functionality, I really only view the mobile version as a task collector throughout the day. I do all scheduling, planning, and management on the desktop and it’s fantastic.
author: cccrstnnn

title: So much potential but too clunky
body: I’ve wanted an app with this functionality for awhile but this falls short on intuitiveness and fluidity. They need to really workshop the experience to justify the price tag. You can’t charge this much and not even try to compete with the fluidity of ToDoist. I know the functionality is different, but the functionality is not useful if it’s too painstaking to use. Also, why do I have to drag every single tasks to the bottom of the list when planning my day? It’s a huge pain if someone is trying to block their day in pomodoros. Just let me add it to the end! And the founder or whoever will literally send you an email every day. Like stop sending emails and fix your app!
author: SpecificNorthwest

title: Miserable login feature
body: This app practically sets you up for failure because when I attempt to revive my account, I never receive the confirmation email (tried twice with two different Gmail accounts  with no success). Then I manually tried to enter an email to make an account and there’s an automated message saying I need to go to the “app website”?? to establish an account. This app IS NOT USER FRIENDLY. You’re better off getting a physical planner and handwriting your tasks. I will never use this app again.
author: mad.bee

title: Calendar takes over 5 seconds to load
body: The calendar takes forever to load, l’ve counted about 5 seconds at times. To make matters worse it often loads the previous days calendar for today. Support refused to fix this, I’ve emailed them multiple times about this
author: Freeto12

title: Great for desktop
body: Very helpful app for the desktop version, but the phone app is still quite limited and not super easy to use. I hope they keep making improvements because I love the concept and use it on my computer all day.
author: Jepahart

title: App performance needs work
body: Sunsama is a helpful product in web, but the app performance needs a lot of work. Input latency is really bad and the app frequently drops or ignored inputs.
author: Ian Geckeler

title: Getting setup NOT ADHD Friendly
body:
You can ONLY get set up on a computer, not with your phone. This is extremely frustrating and by the time I get to a computer I will either not be interested or completely forget.

If it’s this difficult to get started, I can only imagine how difficult and frustrating it will be to use.
author: hbaldwin82308

title: Excellent Workflows, Poor Mobile Execution
body:
Mobile app is near unusable for task editing/addition. I just spent 5+ minutes trying to move three task around on my day, and adjusting the time. Seemingly the only interface for time changes on mobile is touch. Why on earth can I not just edit the field on the task???

Furthermore, new or resized tasks keep appearing/disappearing from the timeline? Did anybody do QA on the iOS app???? This runs as well if not worse than something spat out at a hackathon. The desktop/web app is much more useful, which makes the mobile app all the more disappointing for us subscribers.
author: 0XxXxWxXxX0

title: The best to do app I’ve found
body: I love this app because it can pull in tasks from so many apps and help me create a reasonable workday — email, Apple Reminders, Asana, Clickup, ToDoist and more. It’s gorgeous and works well on phone and desktop. Helps me stay committed to my goals. Absolutely worth the cost. The team is also always willing to listen to feedback.
author: SuzeLeeB

title: App needs work
body: The website is great. The app annoys me to no end though. Every time you put a new event on the calendar it always disappears.
author: Bpatttt

title: Love Sunsama, App Needs Work
body:
As a whole, Sunsama has changed my life. I’m actually productive and my ADHD feels manageable. I would recommend the product to everyone. 

Only downside is the app itself. Web is beautiful and perfect, but the app is glitchy. I try and change dates and tasks just disappear. The app is definitely more limited than desktop which fine, they updated it so you can do a bit more now. But my only quip is the glitches and sometimes the app freezes up. Typically have to close out and reopen for it to all update/fix.

Oh and I wish the calendar view was like the desktop version where it auto inputs your tasks so you can see what it recommends, unless there’s a setting for that which I missed.
author: gamergirlgames123

title: adhd friendly… no alarm alerts reminders?
body: Sincerely love the desktop app. When I do manage to use it that is. The app version I appreciate is truly minimized so you don’t do too much from this tiny screen but why have time based tasks and seemingly avoid implementing a feature to nudge me to do it? I completely forget the app on my phone and sometimes the things I meant to do because of this. Even a sound and ‘task pending’ notification that forces you to open the app and check your tasks would be better than nothing at all.
author: julez23874

title: Amazing product but the App Seriously Needs Help
body:
The desktop version is amazing. The visualization, colors, and UI are extremely helpful for visualizing my day and weeks. I use this in addition to TickTick and now my productivity game is even better. Great for those who are neurodivergent. 

At the same time, I can’t believe the app is so useless. I think it’s time for the product team to add app functionality to the roadmap asap. We can’t carry around our laptops in life.
author: thedom822

title: I don’t get it
body: Way too complicated. Not very intuitive or user friendly. Stuck with a massive list every day if I didn’t do everything or the other option is it all disappears if you don’t do it. My backlog disappeared?! I’m sure the developer finds it intuitive but my brain doesn’t work like theirs. The back end settings are a mess.  Takes too many steps to do basic stuff.
author: The7thBleu

title: Perfect for ADHD and OCD
body: I cannot say enough good things about this app! As someone who struggles with other planners and apps, I’ve found this one to be a perfect fit. There is so much flexibility for every type of processor. I personally prefer using my Google Calendar and tasks, but I’m sure other interfaces work well, too. The time blocking is extraordinarily helpful, as are the 'subtasks'. The different channels allow me to organize my tasks not just in my head, but in something tangible. There are very few presets, and the app is very customizable. The support team is also great. I reached out with a question, and it was answered promptly and thoroughly. For anyone who struggles with executive functioning or brain disorganization, you NEED this app. The subscription is expensive, but very much worth it. I have used dozens of planners in my academic career, and this one has been a lifesaver! I am in my 4th year of college, and I feel so regulated when I use the app. I also love the desktop-to-iPhone app interface. Having ADHD and other mental health challenges can make school planning really difficult, and this app has actually helped. Yay Sunsama!!
author: OddKidRN

title: Lousy onboarding
body: Trying to log in with Google and it keeps asking for username and password.
author: Vonheim

title: App not so good
body: Desktop version is great but app lags in all of the things I’ve added to my schedule. Only half of the things show & sometimes even that’s out of orders. Please fix refresh times on the apps. Sometimes it won’t even show for days & sometimes the stuff I add to my Outlook calendar doesn’t show at all even though it’s synced and working on desktop. Would love for this to work as Sunsama desktop is my life saver.
author: Andreamackie

title: Great Start- Needs more effort toward upgrading user voted requests and improving AI.
body: I tried a few things before this app- one I loved but it was so buggy it was unusable. So I was looking for something new. For the price I feel they should listen to what the USERS want. They do, but there are only 2 current projected user improvements planned. There are also some things you think it should have but doesn’t in the integrations. For asana you can only import task name and due date basically- you can’t import an estimated task completion time. The greatest part though- I have yet to find a single bug. I would also like to see the AI capabilities beefed up as far as scheduling. I have set up timeboxing but it would be cool for AI to schedule my day around meetings with learning technology. I almost went with the other scheduling app that did that but there were reports of bugs in the app 🪳🪳🪳.  I do think the AI that it does have is rather new? Customer service chat turnaround is acceptable.
author: Clickyfrog

title: Hardly Functional
body: I would give the Mac version of this app 5 stars, but the mobile version is terrible. It shows the wrong tasks every time I open the app and I have to force quit to get it to update. The UI feels like a website designed for desktop, not a mobile app, and I often have to tap twice to get things to register, and drag and drop often doesn’t work.
author: loretn11

title: Helpful, intuitive, comprehensive
body: This is so easy to use and has helped me make the most of my time off work. Scheduling and keeping track are not my strong suits so this tool has been powerful for my summer .
author: Eba2026

title: Over a year in and I still love it
body: I’ve been using Sunsama for over a year and I still love it. The only way it could get any better is if there was a Google Docs integration that allowed you to create a task from Google Doc Meeting Notes, but other than that, it’s perfect!
author: Stunningham36

title: Helpful app if you work out of calendar and tasks
body: Very good app, probably my #1 productivity app on my phone for work and life.
author: Crabfisher1982

title: Unusable
body: Entering my username and password merely returns me to the login prompt.  No feedback.   No available faq to fix either.   Simply unusable and a fail.
author: AriCsul

title: Almost great
body: I have fallen in love with this app, but I do wish there were more features for the monthly price. My wish list includes an app for the Apple Watch, timer widget at the Lock Screen, and the ability to view specific task groups in the widget on an app page (e.g. “work stuff”). There are occasional glitches with respect to the timer on iOS, but it’s overall solid.
author: thewxtech

title: It’s how I stay sane in my business
body: There are a lot of productivity apps out there. Pick your poison. I chose this one in 2022 and never looked back. This app is responsible for how I structure my business on a day-to-day basis. It has trained my brain to understand what is possible in a week and what I need to delegate. The dev team constantly brings value through their updates and fantastic customer service. Pay the subscription fee, people. Your time as a business owner is worth it.
author: _Brand_do

title: Needs to integrate AI task list generation to be *perfect*
body: I love this app. It’s the ONLY digital planner I have ever used CONSISTENTLY. I always go back to paper planners because Google Calendar and Anything Microsoft are kryptonite for my ADHD. It’s WAY too easy to delete appointments, lose emails, and the task management tools are useless. I love that Sunsuma is visual and hand holds you through planning. you can move tasks around. undone tasks are bounced to the next day or a backlog so they never disappear. I also love having weekly goals, subtasks and the ability to attach weekly goals to specific tasks. There are lots of integrations including email and calendars so all your work stays synched. You can turn emails into actionable tasks. The only serious problem I’ve had so far is the fact that I still need to open up chat GPT to create a to-do list from my overwhelmed brain dump. It would be great if there was a built in AI that would build and organize your weekly work plan, complete with subtasks, for you. The thing about ADHD is that you CAN’T MAKE THE LIST IN THE FIRST PLACE without help. Sunsuma was underutilized whenever I had list-writers-block and would sit unused for a few days. Once I started using chat to make my to-do lists I really started to appreciate Sunsuma and get the most out of the features. AI task list generation and scheduling would make it the perfect digital planner for me, and I will I Use it forever.  I’d also love Airtable integration if that is possible.
author: Nobranier

title: Want to love it, very glitchy
body: Overall the best designed app for the functionality I’m looking for, just wish it actually worked as intended. Lots of issues with the iPad version— very sensitive and I end up rescheduling or moving events when I’m simply trying to scroll down the page. Lots of integration issues with ToDoIst, which I rely on a lot, so if this isn’t working well, it kind of defeats the purpose of me using this app. Needs a lot of work to iron out these issues— if that could be done, this would be my go-to app.
author: lp104

title: iOS app is unusable
body:
I noticed that a lot of reviews are about features in the desktop app that aren't available on iOS. Well that isn't my complaint. I don't mind setting things up at my desk band using the app for quick updates. 

My issue is with the fact that the app crashes every time I try to do anything with it. And worse the website forces me back to the app if I try to use chrome or safari.

Please at a minimum stop the website from forcing the mobile app to open until the bugs in the mobile app are fixed. I don't want to have to cancel and set something else up but I can't keep paying for an app that I can't use on the go.
author: SGTMcClain

title: A companion to my LIFE!
body:
I am a time management coach and Sunsama one of the best digital tools out their. I have been a user for almost two years now. Some of the reviews here talk about the app not being great and please remember - their language is a “companion to the desktop” … not an app on its own! It’s important to remember that going into using this tool or considering it. 

That being said, the past couple of weeks the companion (app) has been funky. My calendar doesn’t sync properly or takes a while to sync. I use Sunsama as my master overview because it connects all my calendars but it hasn’t been doing that successfully lately. I hope the bugs can be fixed soon. 

The CEO sends weekly emails with tutorials and fun insights into time management and I love it. The access to him / to ask him questions is such a breath of fresh air compared to other apps where you don’t even know who made it. Sunsama people are GOOD people and they constantly are seeking to improve the tool (I do think they could put more emphasis on improving the app/companion though)
author: mmmmmteee

title: Sunsama Makes Me Better
body:
By far the most impactful tool/app/system I’ve tried in the past few years. 

If it clicks for you, there’s a learning curve, it is a life changer / saver. 

I balance my time, achieve my personal/professional goals, integrate into work and personal systems with everything from automatic, accurate, asynchronous daily recaps sent to teammates across the world to pick up the torch

to helping break down Mountains into molehills for personal pursuits, or logging and resurfacing a random article/idea  

Sunsama on desktop, web, and app is 🎯
author: doubledee22

title: Desktop is great but crazy expensive
body: The mobile apps for both phone and tablets are absolute trash. Seriously useless which is wild considering sunsama costs $20 a month. I love the desktop app but they don’t have student, military, healthcare, no discounts whatsoever which is ridiculous to me. No other productivity app costs this much per month.
author: GoldenEssenceHEC

title: I truly wanted to give this app a chance
body:
The app sounds great, if you can actually get in the app and use it. Unfortunately right now, there seems to be a lot of bugs that need worked out. 
Issues are:
The app and the website are not currently talking with each other. Is one issue I see right away.
If you try sighting up with a google account, watch out. It doesn’t work. Doesn’t matter how you try to confirm you identify, it doesn’t work. None of the ways it says it will work actually work. Such as being able to put in your passcode, my iPad didn’t prompt at all for that. I only received one email from google, even after I sand yes it was safe. It still didn’t work. 

I know that the developers are not going to want to hear this, but my husband actually works in IT, so I have learned that when an app is not fully tested well, there is going to be issues. It is clear this app, was not fully tested out well. Because there are major issues. 
This app needs pulled, and further work needs done in the development side of this app, before it should be re- released back out to the public. 

This is my fair and honest review. From someone who is looking for a good digital planner, who currently uses a paper and pencil. 
Please pull this app, and work out all the bugs, they are bad! So this app will also work with the website.
author: Gamingmama79

title: Impossible Set Up
body: Tried signing in using Google. Google took me in circles for 15 minutes not accepting any of my authentication in spite of them being right. Then I get through that gauntlet to tell me no account exists. Tried creating with email “id already taken”. So which is it?! No support resources to be found anywhere and they apparently just don’t have a team. Nearly an hour wasted - I’m done.
author: ArmoredBallerina

title: Overpriced
body: Great quality but not great enough to expect nearly $200 a year. What happened to the one time purchase options! If you insist on doing a monthly subscription instead of offering a one time purchase plan then instead of $20 a month make it a reasonable price. I would be willing to pay no more than $10 a month for ANY app no matter what features or how amazing it is. Especially considering there is much cheaper and even free options that one can now just use split screen with their Google calendar and basically do the same thing just not in one app.
author: Butterthedragonfly

title: Worth every penny
body: I did the free trial and then let it lapse for a day or two before taking the plunge. As others have mentioned, the mobile app is slightly limited (but getting better!) but holy god, the combo of the desktop + mobile app system has honestly changed my life. The clarity it’s given me to bring together all my objectives and tasks so I know exactly what I’m doing (and also track my time doing it) is worth the annual cost. I use this with the free version of ToDoist and my cal (my personal iCal synced though Google cal + my work Google cal) and have gotten more focused work completed in the past month or two than I have this entire year. So happy I found Sunsama and am excited to see what the dev team has in store!
author: Nittgyytbs

title: Literally my entire life
body:
I’m not reviewing the mobile app, as I barely use the mobile version other than checking my schedule. I plan and manage everything on my desktop. 
Holy cow, is this my literal lifeline. I used it a while ago for the free trial and loved it but decided it was too expensive as a college student. But a year later research and university ramped up and I need to be way more intentional with my time. I remembered how great it was and I’ve been using it since and let me tell you. My workload? Double than normal. My stress levels? Halved. I actually know when I’m going to do things, and plan them out in a way that I know works for ME. This is not an all-in-one app, though, and shouldn’t be treated as such. I keep a notion page for deadlines for projects and due dates for homeworks, and then come to Sunsama to plan how I’m gonna tackle it all. Yes it’s expensive, but I would honestly give up two meals a month to make up for the price tag, that’s how much I’ve come to rely on it. 10/10 for a busy stem girl
author: birdlover1001

title: NO APPLE WATCH SUPPORT
body: We want Apple Watch support!
author: Mahdi5264

title: Autism friendly, one of my favorite systems, S Tier
body: I have autism, and Sunsama is one of the only systems I've tried that can work for me for extended periods of time. Even though it's not meant for habit tracking, putting my routines in here and being able to check minuscule things off on my phone is like the only way I can stay on track. Otherwise, I can't mentally keep track of what small action goes between each daily task, or even which things to do first. I've had a lot of trouble with being late and unprepared and overwhelmed because of that but Sunsama makes it so easy for me to see what comes next after every little step.
author: ADLP32

title: Overpriced
body: Remember the days when you could straight out by an app and Microsoft 360 and just own it and you were willing to pay a premium one time price? It seems those days are over and there’s no way I would pay $16 a month for this app after I downloaded it and checked it out. That’s $192 a year. Let us know when you get the price down to something reasonable for what you’re offering.
author: Dbo #13 global

title: No mention in the App Store this is a paid product
body: It seems like a nicely designed product, but it is quite expensive per month, with no mention of a monthly charge list in the App Store
author: eimbier

title: Elegant
body: Beautiful and immensely practical companion app to a beautiful and immensely practical core program/application. Still in the beginning stages of trying it out as someone with severe ADHD, but so far it shows a wonderful amount of promise and the interface itself is gorgeous without distracting and streamlined but powerful. At first I worried it’d be too expensive but the more I learn and explore and implement these workflows the more I see where that money goes. The creators should be very proud of themselves, and I can’t wait to see how Sunsama evolves.
author: Microfoo77

title: One of my absolute favorite apps of all time
body: Sunsama absolutely revolutionized how I organize and plan my day. I love that it optimizes for shortcuts. It integrates beautifully with so many other tools I use. The timers and stats have been incredibly helpful.I just adore absolutely everything about this app. I primarily use the desktop but often use my phone if I’m on the go. I’ve even started using Sunsama for my personal tasks. It’s so thoughtfully designed and I love the ability to customize the colors in the app.
author: Lynette D

title: Changes to the app
body: This was a 5 star app for me, however, when I went to sign up for a subscription things changed a bit. I noticed that when I enter a task now an actual time has to be put on each task and once that time passes the task is no longer in its place. I think this is because when you arrange your tasks it’s delayed in updating and could revert back. I prefer the task to remain and then roll over if not completed. Also, using a desktop for the app wasn’t required previously and I’m not sure why that’s a thing and also should be optional but it’s not terrible I guess. I loved the app and recommended it in my ADHD groups because it was so great, but with the changes I’m not sure how anyone else will feel.
author: richardbucket

title: Companion app to an amazing piece of software
body:
The companion app continues to improve over time and they even have an iPad version which works pretty good. I am rating this on the overall software capabilities and not just the iOS app. Overall without the companion and additional web/desktop app, my work/life balance would be much harder to achieve. 

This is not a to do list app, this is a daily and weekly planner app.
author: Rtloeffler

title: Amazing, except for one big item and one small item
body: I’ve tried some other planners before and between them being clunky due to them not being designed for what Sunsama does. Based on the small amount of time that I’ve had using this, I am pleased generally with the functionality offered. However there is one really large omission that prevents me from giving it a five star review: there is no integration that I have been able to find with iCloud calendar which is what I use for the majority of events (it is possible to overcome this in some ways, but this is a feature that would be tremendous to add). The other thing is that it’s annoying that you are forced to sign in using either google or outlook when I’d prefer to use Sign in with Apple or just create an account directly with Sunsama. I’m still a trial customer but I’m intending to modify my review once the trial ends to see if anything new has come up from my use of the application.
author: monsieurmétro

title: Tried everything and this is the app that finally changed my life
body: I love this app.  It’s the first app that works for me after many sad failed attempts to use productivity apps like asana click up Trello etc
author: nicknameanynickname123

title: Widgets are no gone??
body: See title. iPhone 14 Pro. Latest iOS.
author: Jpuritz

title: Great product, NO customer support
body:
If you want to commit to it, need to be cautious. I signed up and had some issue, sent an email to support. After two emails, no response at all. 

Great product otherwise.
author: pengrus

title: Good App. Poorly Priced
body:
I recently started a two-week trial of Sunsama  after using Todoist, Notion, and Things 3. Despite the lack of extensive online discussions about Sunsama, its mention in a YouTube video piqued my interest. However, the $20 monthly fee initially deterred me. Considering I've invested similarly in Asana and Notion for their unique robust features, I decided to give  Sunsama a try.  While impressed with the app, I find the subscription cost steep compared to its competitors. I believe a lower price point, perhaps around $10, would be more reasonable and competitive. 

To the Sunsama team, as a fellow business owner, I understand the challenge of pricing. Your product has potential, but its current price may hinder its success. Consider a more competitive pricing strategy. For context, Todoist is at $5, and Asana at $20. Sunsama surpasses Todoist but doesn’t match the advanced features of Asana or NotionAI. A fair price would be between $7 to $10. I urge you to quickly adjust your pricing to better reflect its market position. Despite this, I appreciate the app's design and functionality, earning it three stars from me. A pricing reevaluation could greatly enhance its market success.
author: Shaner702

title: Phone functionality is a bummer
body: I love this platform so much. It’s been life changing for me, but I often work from my phone and it’s mind blowing how limited planning from the mobile app is. When I’m around my computer regularly, it’s the best thing in my life, but once I have a stretch of time working from mobile, all momentum goes down the drain. I am hoping for this feature to be released soon because it is starting to feel silly to pay so much when I can’t use it properly half of the time.
author: Urrrggh

title: A work in progress
body: Great when it works. Repeatedly crashes and could be a remarkable app. But it’s just not ready for prime time yet.
author: Remax100

title: Almost the best app out there
body: The one thing I feel this application is missing is the ability to reply to emails from the platform. It’s great to be able to integrate my emails to review and pull task from them, but the ability to reply to emails would set this experience apart from other softwares.
author: 01010101monty

title: 5 stars for the Mac Desktop app
body:
The Mac desktop app is the way to really use this platform. iOS app is more of a companion. I’ve used tons of planning and taks management tools and this is by far the more useful. It’s an extremely logical and helpful way to plan your goals and achieve them.

Small nit - the shutdown flow can definitely be improved. It’s pretty basic with the questions asked and just the blank canvass. Suggest a way to measure how the day went and potentially see over time and on the calendar view how well individual days have gone according to plan.
author: dabears07

title: Disappointing
body: Unnecessary updates, poor communication, and rude customer service comments lost me as a customer.
author: Untitled.jpg

title: Great app & Team
body: Love the app and team behind it. Its been incredibly helpful. Ive used it all. Basecamp. Things. Todoist. Obsidian. Notion. Google cal. Sunsama is perfect and for me its paired with notion.
author: Hahajxjejxhoajabx

title: Great time blocker, but a few areas for improvement
body:
First off, I really do love using this to organize my time and plan out my day across all my different to do lists. It helps me manage my day tremendously and I have not found a better alternative so far. I also understand that due to the complexity, the app is meant to be more complimentary to the process you complete on the desktop version. 

However, for the price you pay, a few things would make this an ultimate standout for me: 

1.) more integration options with other apps (for me specifically, tick tick instead of only Todoist as a to do list app option). Right now, the limited number of integrations (while streamlined and easy) - operates under an “all or nothing” approach where you must use the apps they offer in order for this to be useful. 

2.) WIDGETS! If the goal is to help you streamline the never ending sources of professional, personal, and other tasks into one clear source of “truth” with a plan…and with the amount we spend on mobile, if the app cannot operate effectively as a stand alone product - then widgets would help resolve that issue on my end. 

It would offer visually effective overviews of your schedules, progress, objectives etc. in a way that makes sense for the specific individual and greatly help with motivation throughout the day, even when away from the “desktop”. A huge reason I honestly preferred tick tick over to doist as a personal to do list task manager was due to its effective widgets, so I was bummed when I couldn’t integrate it into Sunsama. 

3.) better ways to move, re-reschedule, delete etc. with multiple items at a time.

-  For example, right now it has you plan or look at two days at a time. And if you are past the recommended number of hours in a day - it will recommend you move those items to next week (no option to reschedule “one day” from that screen). 
- Also, if you planned out a week in advance and later need to shift things around, it would be great to be able to group items and move them all together (or select multiple at a time). Sometimes items are related but not grouped into sub tasks, and it becomes extremely frustrating to move and stroll over 1 task at a time.
- more clarity about what “deleting” does and also if a day went by but you didn’t “check” off a task. Does it move it back to the specific inbox of the task manager you pulled it from?  Does it go into an archive list where you then forget about it? Depending on the situation I’ve seen it all happen, and it would be great to have ore clarity upfront.

author: SamaraLloyd

title: Misleading 👎🏼
body:
Saw some other users complain about the lack of clarity on pricing and usage, etc. Hope this review helps y’all :) 

In the App Description and the Information section, neither indicate whether or not this app is Free, One-time Payment, or Subscription-only. So, I presumed it was Free. However, I cannot use the app because it says I need a company’s email address or Sunsama account to receive the signup link and code in order to start using the app. Stating that this app is a companion to the Desktop version is all fine and well, but it still doesn’t answer the above about pricing, signing up, and so on. 

I went to their website and, after some browsing, I finally found answers: 
• App is free to download, but you will not be able to use it unless you have a Sunsama account. 
• Pricing: $20.00 USD per month/billed monthly, or $16.00 USD per month/billed annually. 
• There is no difference between the Free Trial version and the Subscription/Paid version, thus you get the full experience during the trial period. 
• They do not charge you after the free trial. According to some of the screenshots on their website… it appears that after the trial ends, you are locked out of your account until you choose a payment plan, and then you can pick up where you left off. 

When in doubt, read others’ reviews and check an app/company’s website for further info, especially for Pricing and FAQs.  Have a great day! シ
author: pebblecrunch

title: Underdeveloped mobile app for a pricey membership
body:
I wouldn't go so far as to say the mobile app is "useless", but it is surprisingly underfeatured for how costly Sunsama is ($20/month). The mobile app is not "minimal so you can focus" or anything like that. It is underfeatured. You can't see more than one day at a time. You can't really meaningfully alter your schedule. There is no local cache that I can tell, so if your phone isn't getting wifi or data signal, tough! It assumes you are regularly at a desktop computer to do your planning ritual, but I'm sorry, that's not how the workplace is in 2022! To design your whole app system around that assumption seems naive! If this was a free / cheaper app I'd be a lot more lenient about this, but full individual membership is $20 per MONTH. 

Sunsama overall is thoughtfully designed with a growing catalog of useful integrations, so that part is well worth the price - but other productivity apps of comparable price have more fully featured mobile apps comparable to their desktop counterparts (Trello, Smartsheet, Asana). I know it is a new app that is in continuing development so I am hoping they make the mobile app more useful soon… but for the time being, beware!
